scanner.title: Scanner Input
whereToLook: Make sure you created a Scanner object using System.in.
Read the number of tasks completed with nextInt() and store it in your tasks variable.
Print the prompt text exactly as shown in the README before reading the input.

conditionals.title: Choosing the Percentage
whereToLook: A switch on tasks with one case per row of the table works well; so does an if-else-if chain.
If you use a switch, end each case with break so the next case does not also run.
Make sure the percentage you display comes from the variable your decision set, not a fixed value.

validation.title: Rejecting an Invalid Number
whereToLook: Only 0 through 5 are valid. Every other number prints the invalid message.
In a switch, default catches every value that no case matches.
When the number is invalid, do not print the score line.

tests.name: Displays the input prompt
tests.expectedOutput: How many tasks did the astronaut complete?
tests.message: Your program should print the prompt 'How many tasks did the astronaut complete?' before reading input.

tests.name: 0 tasks completed
tests.message: When 0 tasks are completed, the astronaut's score should be 0 percent. Check the condition in your if statement for 0 tasks.

possibleErrors.message: Your output shows 100 percent even though 0 tasks were completed. Make sure your conditional logic looks at the value entered instead of always displaying the same percentage.

tests.name: 1 task completed
tests.message: When 1 task is completed, the astronaut's score should be 10 percent. Check the condition in your if / else if chain for 1 task.

tests.name: 2 tasks completed
tests.message: When 2 tasks are completed, the astronaut's score should be 25 percent. Check the condition in your if / else if chain for 2 tasks.

tests.name: 3 tasks completed
tests.message: When 3 tasks are completed, the astronaut's score should be 45 percent. Check the condition in your if / else if chain for 3 tasks.

possibleErrors.message: 3 tasks printed the 4-task score. If you used a switch, check that case 3 ends with break.

tests.name: 4 tasks completed
tests.message: When 4 tasks are completed, the astronaut's score should be 70 percent. Check the condition in your if / else if chain for 4 tasks.

tests.name: 5 tasks completed
tests.message: When 5 tasks are completed, the astronaut's score should be 100 percent. Check the condition in your if / else if chain for 5 tasks.

possibleErrors.message: Your output shows 0 percent even though 5 tasks were completed. Make sure every branch of your conditional logic sets the percentage correctly.

tests.name: Rejects a negative number
tests.expectedOutput: Invalid number of tasks. Enter 0 through 5.
tests.message: Numbers below 0 should print "Invalid number of tasks. Enter 0 through 5."

possibleErrors.message: Your program printed a score line for an invalid number. Print only the invalid message.

tests.name: Rejects a number above 5
tests.expectedOutput: Invalid number of tasks. Enter 0 through 5.
tests.message: Numbers above 5 should print "Invalid number of tasks. Enter 0 through 5."

possibleErrors.message: Your program printed a score line for an invalid number. Print only the invalid message.
